title: Give every invoice in the chain its own number

blocks.text: A retail chain issues invoice numbers from one sequence for the whole company, and every branch's tills call `issue(...)` on their own branch's `Branch` object. The finance team has two complaints. The audit found pairs of invoices with the same number, issued seconds apart by different branches, and journal lines with their numbers out of order. And on the morning a new branch opened, every till in the chain froze for as long as the new branch took to load its settings from head office.

Write `issue(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/Branch.java`. Each call takes the next number of the company's sequence, writes it to the journal with the branch's name and the customer, and returns it. With any number of tills in any number of branches calling it at once, no number is issued twice, the journal gets its lines one at a time and in number order, and no till waits for a branch that is being opened. About five lines in total, and you may add a field.
The tests use journals and settings loaders that hold a call open, so they can see who waits for whom.

cases.says: numbers issued by different branches follow one company-wide sequence, and the journal gets each number with its branch and customer, in order
opening a branch twice returns the same branch, which issues numbers
while one branch is writing its number to the journal, another branch's till waits instead of issuing
while one till of a branch is writing its number to the journal, another till of the same branch waits
a till issues a number while a new branch is still loading its settings

origin.section: synchronized Locks an Object, and Excludes Only Code That Locks the Same One

concepts: A monitor other code can reach, such as this, a Class object or a string literal, lets that code stall yours; a private final lock can be taken only by the class.
synchronized excludes only code that locks the same object; synchronized (new Object()) or an instance lock guarding state shared between instances excludes nothing.
